blocking.section: Recommended exact spec diff: §8.3 opening requirement, exact-entry exception and legacy handling

steps.claim: Epsilon expressions use exact rational arithmetic. An eps-independent expression evaluating to zero is an exact native match for §17 item 9, and §4.4 requires the exact phase-fixed operation at epsilon zero.
The diff requires a realisation_model for every expression-valued epsilon, but subsequently permits exact entries to omit it and denote the exact opcode.

Take conformance/fixtures/controlled-action-09/target.json and replace gates[0].epsilon with {"op":"-","args":[1,1]}, leaving realisation_model absent. The epsilon is exactly zero and independent of eps, while its syntax is expression-valued.

The opening rule requires a model for this entry; the exact-entry exception permits omission. Consequently the diff does not consistently determine whether the exact controlled-X obligation is checkable or missing-model unchecked.

blocking.fix: In §8.3, replace the opening requirement and reconcile the exact-entry and migration sentences as follows: “A native entry MUST supply a versioned realisation_model if its epsilon can evaluate to a nonzero value in an admitted resolved context. An entry whose epsilon is independent of eps and evaluates to zero in every admitted context MAY omit the model and then denotes the exact §4.4 opcode, including global phase and controlled form. A supplied model MUST agree with that exact operation in every zero-epsilon context and satisfy the advertised bound otherwise. For legacy entries lacking a required model, missing-model unchecked reporting applies only to nonzero-epsilon contexts.” The 1−1 fixture must remain exact and checkable without a model. For a legacy X entry with epsilon={"var":"c"} covering c=0..1, c=0 denotes exact X without a model; c=1 remains missing-model unchecked. Alternatively, require models for every expression syntax and explicitly restrict the omission exception to literal zero, documenting that validation change. Prefer the value-based repair, which preserves the existing exact-entry convention.

suggestions: In §8.3, state: “A channel-only model supports channel comparison; an operator-norm claim requires a phase-fixed realised unitary. Model normalization does not itself establish §4.4 accuracy or an inverse.” For example, Ch(X)=Ch(−X) cannot establish numerical bound zero against X. Retaining the existing §4.4 obligations is preferable for this K repair; admitting general nonunitary native gates would instead require an explicit amendment defining their accuracy and reversal semantics.

In §8.3, state: “Model instantiation uses the matched entry’s resolved k, c, eps and angle values. An explicit operand-to-wire map converts the model basis to §12.1’s controls-first allocation basis.” This makes the existing reconstruction obligation concrete for accuracy-dependent models and avoids confusing §8.3’s template control order with the certificate matrix order.

For the initial versioned model schema, publish canonical positive and negative examples. Include exact X without a model, X and −X models under one outer control, and a malformed Kraus list. Expected results: equal uncontrolled channels, opposite controlled Bell off-diagonal entries ±1/2, rejection of the −X bound-zero numerical claim, and rejection of a non-trace-preserving model.
path_to_accept: Replace the conflicting expression-valued and exact-entry rules with B1’s value-based rule, including the stated outcomes for identically-zero and mixed-control epsilon expressions. No source or reference-catalog change is required.
summary: The defect, phase witness and hash analysis are sound. One contract contradiction prevents applying the diff verbatim: expression syntax is treated as requiring a model even when epsilon is exactly zero, while the same diff permits exact entries to omit it.
